The drag model also failed. The mouse clicks so far haven't done anything (all no_impact). Note: the batch stopped after the first no_impact — meaning the second MOUSE(47,52) might not have been executed! The explore batch stops after the first no_impact. So the drag test was only a single click. Hmm, the result shows no_impact: True, and the executed action is MOUSE(19,45). So the second click wasn't executed.
Let me use intent='solve' to force both clicks. Or test each click individually.
Also, I should test ACTION7, which I haven't tested yet. And SPACE too.
Let me think about the design from a different angle. This is a mirror puzzle. In L1, the arrow keys moved the piece. In L2, the arrow keys move the wall. What distinguishes them?
In L1: the piece B is on the left side of the wall. In L2: the piece B is on the right side of the wall.
Maybe the arrow keys always move the object on the left side of the wall closest to the wall? In L1, B (left side, closest) moved. In L2, the closest object on the left side is c (the mirror)... but c is derived. Unless c is not derived and is actually a real object, and what's derived is... no wait, in L2 when the wall moved left by 3, c moved left by 6, and B didn't move. If c were a real object and the arrow keys moved "the closest object on the left side," c should have moved 3 left, not 6. It moved 6 = exactly the mirror transformation. So c is derived from B and the wall.
Hmm, wait, maybe it's actually the opposite: in L2, the arrow keys move the wall, and in L1 they moved the piece... what if the rule is "the arrow keys move the object closest to the wall (on either side)"? L1: B is at cols 18-26, distance to wall (30-32) = 4. The only object. L2: B is at 45-59, distance to wall (33-35) = 10; c is at 9-23, distance = 10. A tie! And the wall itself is... hmm, the wall moved.
Or maybe the rule is "the arrow keys move the object closest to the wall, and if it's the wall, the wall moves"? In L2, c and B are equidistant (10 each). Tie → the wall moves? That's a stretch.
Let me look at the actual L2 LEFT behavior more carefully. Before LEFT: wall 36-38 (center 37), B 45-59, c 6-20. After LEFT: wall 33-35 (center 34), B 45-59, c 9-23. So the wall moved 3 left, c moved 3 right (mirror), B unchanged.
And L2 DOWN/UP: no effect (the wall can't move vertically).
So in L2, the wall is the "active" object. In L1, the piece was active. What determines which is active? Maybe the side of the wall the piece is on? In L1 the piece is on the left; in L2 the piece is on the right. Maybe the "active" object is the one on the left side of the wall? In L1, B (left) is active. In L2, the objects on the left side are c and yellow; the wall is... no, the wall is the wall.
Hmm, wait. Maybe I'm thinking about it backwards. What if the arrow keys move the wall, and in L1 the "wall" was actually... no, in L1 the wall never moved.
Let me reconsider: maybe there's a selection mechanism, and the initially selected object differs per level. In L1, the piece was selected. In L2, the wall is selected. And the mouse click selects an object. My clicks on B didn't change the selection... or did they? After clicking B, DOWN had no effect — but if the wall is still selected, DOWN has no effect anyway. So I can't tell whether the click changed the selection. I need a discriminating test: click B, then LEFT. If the selection moved to B, B should move 3 left (and c should mirror). If the wall is still selected, the wall should move 3 left.
Let me do that: MOUSE(19,45) with intent='solve' (to force execution), then LEFT, and check.
Actually, the explore batch stops on the first no_impact — the click itself is no_impact (a selection change might not count as a board change... or does it? If the selection is rendered as a highlight, the board would change). The click was no_impact → no visible selection highlight. So the selection isn't rendered. The discriminating test: click B, then LEFT, and see what moves.
Let me run it with intent='solve'.
